J12-05.fixture: Cruz Azul vs Atletico San Luis

learning: The economic selector improved the objective from raw probability ranking to price-aware EV ranking. This rule was frozen before J12 settlement and should remain unchanged until enough prospective evidence exists to justify a new selector version.

The two largest apparent leg-level proxy edges were Atletico San Luis to score >=1 (+23.61%) and Puebla to score >=1 (+6.99%); both failed. This is not enough to reject the signals, but it highlights a structural concern: MARKET_PROXY_V1 derives team-goal prices from 1X2 via an independent-Poisson fit, so extreme model-vs-proxy edges may partly be proxy misspecification rather than true market edge.
Tijuana to score >=1 carried +14.21% proxy EV and hit. Therefore a single jornada gives mixed evidence on team-to-score disagreement; do not create a direction-specific penalty from J12 alone.
P1 had +37.67% ticket-level proxy EV and lost; P2 had +22.28% and won. Outcome still cannot validate or invalidate EV in one observation.

P3 was slightly negative-EV (-0.97%) and lost even though two of its three legs hit. The EV-disciplined counterfactual avoided this 40 MXN ticket and now leads the forced track 1078.95 vs 975.05. This difference is a useful diagnostic but sample size is only two jornadas.
Legacy MODEL_ONLY went 3/3 again. Preserve the legacy comparator; do not use this streak to claim economic edge because its historical exact prices are not the same experiment.

From J13, continue logging exact-market audit error = exact archived target-market odds minus proxy odds whenever temporally defensible. Do not promote proxy-EV as a trusted edge measure until the proxy itself is validated across a sufficiently large set of exact-market observations.

J12 is researcher outcome-exposed. It can advance mechanical bankroll accounting but must be excluded from blind feature/context promotion. J13 must use pregame-only discovery sources before selection to restore clean researcher blindness.
